notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no commentary notes for you on Ecclesiastes 9.

My first attempt to open the source pages failed with an error saying I had no tool calls left for this turn. As a result, I didn't read anything: not Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin or the NET Bible notes. Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So any notes I wrote now would be made up, and they would have no real URLs behind them.

If you start a new turn (for example, reply "continue"), I'll try again. This is the plan:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Ecclesiastes 9, then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, then Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus Reformed and Baptist pages (Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Spurgeon) and Lutheran pages (LCMS, 1517). I'll look especially at:
   - vv. 1–3: everyone sharing one fate, and God's sovereignty
   - vv. 5–6 and 10: what the dead know, and Sheol
   - vv. 7–9: enjoying life, and "God has already approved your works"
3. **Other views:**
   - Translation and scholarly notes from netbible.org and bibleodyssey.org
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings, including Church Fathers on newadvent.org
   - Any pages on these sites about how vv. 5 and 10 are used in "soul sleep" debates, or how vv. 7–9 are used in prosperity teaching

Each point will come with its URL.
